question: What is the primary goal of health promotion?

options.A: Enabling people to increase control over and improve their health
options.B: Providing free medications to rural communities
options.C: Treating acute diseases in hospital settings

explanation: Health promotion focuses on empowering individuals and communities to manage and better their overall well-being rather than just curing sickness. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h1)

question: How does health promotion differ from basic disease treatment?

options.A: It relies entirely on expensive surgical interventions
options.B: It focuses on environmental conditions and empowerment rather than just fixing illness
options.C: It is handled exclusively by doctors in private clinics
options.D: It only applies to children and elderly populations

explanation: While disease treatment steps in after sickness occurs, health promotion looks at the bigger social and living conditions that keep people well in the first place. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why is community participation essential in health promotion?

options.A: People must be involved in identifying their own health needs and solutions
options.B: Foreign donors require it before releasing any funds
options.C: It ensures that nurses do not have to work in rural areas
options.D: It guarantees that the government will provide free vehicles

explanation: Active community involvement ensures that health programs actually match what the people need and care about, leading to better success rates. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h2)

question: What does the principle of equity mean in public health?

options.A: Fair distribution of health resources to close gaps between different groups
options.B: Giving every single hospital the exact same amount of cash
options.C: Providing identical medical treatments to every patient regardless of age
options.D: Ensuring doctors earn the same salary as community health workers

explanation: Equity means giving fair opportunities and resources based on need so that everyone has a fair chance at good health, especially vulnerable populations. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which landmark document formally launched the modern health promotion movement in 1986?
explanation: The Ottawa Charter of 1986 defined the core strategies for health promotion on a global scale. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h3)

question: What was the big shift in thinking brought by the Ottawa Charter?

options.A: Transferring all health responsibilities from governments to private individuals
options.B: Mandating that every village must build a modern tertiary hospital
options.C: Focusing exclusively on pharmaceutical distribution in developing nations
options.D: Shifting focus away from just treating sickness toward social and environmental living conditions

explanation: You've got this! The Charter expanded our understanding of health beyond just hospitals and doctors to include living conditions, policies, and community environments. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h3)

question: Giving routine childhood immunizations falls under which level of prevention?
explanation: Primary prevention stops a disease or condition from occurring in the first place through measures like vaccination and health education. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h4)

question: A community health nurse organizes a blood pressure screening exercise at the local market. What level of prevention is this?
explanation: Screenings are designed for early detection of health problems so that intervention can start before complications develop. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major social determinant of health in Nigeria?

options.A: Availability of clean water and rural infrastructure
options.B: The brand of stethoscope used by attending physicians
options.D: Household income and overall poverty levels

explanation: Medical equipment brand does not determine public health outcomes, whereas income, education, and water supply profoundly affect community well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h5)

question: How does poor rural road infrastructure negatively impact healthcare delivery in Nigeria?

options.A: It automatically lowers the birth rate in urban centers
options.B: It causes nurses to abandon their profession entirely
options.C: It delays emergency medical referrals from primary clinics to tertiary hospitals
options.D: It prevents international organizations from sending financial reports

explanation: Bad roads and difficult transport make moving critical emergency cases, such as obstructed labor or severe trauma, extremely slow and dangerous. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which health promotion approach focuses primarily on giving people information so they can make informed personal choices?
explanation: The educational approach centers on knowledge sharing and building life skills to help people make healthier choices for themselves. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the main objective of the empowerment approach in health promotion?

options.A: Ensuring that government officials make all health decisions for citizens
options.B: Forcing communities to build modern hospitals using their own unpaid labor
options.C: Helping people gain the confidence and skills to take control of their own health
options.D: Relying solely on foreign pharmaceutical donations

explanation: Empowerment focuses on building self-reliance so communities can advocate for their own needs and solve local health problems. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why is it ineffective to impose health programs on a community without their input?

options.A: The community will likely ignore or abandon the program because it does not match their real needs
options.B: It violates international aviation laws regarding medical supplies
options.C: It requires too many computers for local health workers
options.D: Local government chairmen are legally forbidden to assist

explanation: If people do not feel ownership or see the relevance of a health initiative, they will not sustain it once outside support stops. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h7)

question: A nurse wants to improve sanitation in a rural village. What is the best first step based on community empowerment principles?

options.A: Hold a town hall meeting to listen to community members discuss their main sanitation concerns
options.B: Write an academic paper about rural hygiene without visiting the village
options.C: Order all residents to clean their compounds under police supervision
options.D: Wait for international donors to build modern public toilets

explanation: Starting with dialogue ensures that the community leads the process and addresses problems they actually care about. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h7)

question: When a community health nurse speaks up for marginalized villagers who lack clean water, what nursing role is being demonstrated?
explanation: Advocacy involves speaking up, defending, and fighting for the rights and health needs of vulnerable or voiceless populations. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h8)

question: Why is cultural humility crucial for a community health nurse?

options.A: It helps the nurse respect local beliefs and build trust with community members
options.B: It prevents the nurse from ever needing to wash their hands
options.C: It ensures the nurse receives a higher salary from the government
options.D: It allows the nurse to diagnose complex surgical conditions instantly

explanation: Understanding and respecting local traditions breaks down barriers and encourages people to accept health advice and services. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of evaluating a health promotion program?

options.A: To increase the cost of purchasing imported drugs
options.B: To check if the program achieved its goals and used resources effectively
options.C: To prove that the government needs no further assistance
options.D: To find reasons to dismiss junior healthcare staff

explanation: Evaluation helps determine what worked well, what failed, and how future health interventions can be improved. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h9)

question: Which of the following is a major systemic challenge facing health promotion programs in Nigeria?

options.A: An extreme surplus of modern medical equipment in rural areas
options.B: Too many well-funded hospitals with no patients to treat
options.C: Brain drain of skilled healthcare professionals leaving the country
options.D: Zero interest from local communities in improving their health

explanation: The migration of experienced doctors and nurses abroad significantly weakens local healthcare delivery systems and health promotion efforts. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h9)
